title: Throughput reliability banding and GPU fallthrough triage playbook for dedicated requests
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: Sales and support get ad-hoc inbound requests for reserved GPU pools with inconsistent information: vague throughput targets, unknown burst patterns, and ambiguous GPU-class preference. Current intake yields long back-and-forth with customers and engineering, slowing onboarding and increasing mismatch risk (wrong GPU class, insufficient SLA).

Goal: Create a practical triage playbook that product managers and solutions engineers can use during intake calls to produce a recommended SLA band, reserved throughput profile, GPU-family recommendation, and scaling policy stub that engineering can reliably implement. The playbook must be operationalizable (templates, scoring rubric, example answers) and reduce average intake→proposal time by 50% for enterprise dedicated asks.

Scope: Non-bug dedicated capacity requests requiring contractual reserved throughput and SLA targets. Includes initial qualification, triage scoring, GPU fallthrough guidance (e.g., prefer A100 quantized vs H100 mixed precision), and policy for graceful degradation and burst handling. Excludes pricing/legal negotiations and deep performance benchmarking (which will be a separate eng request).

Why now: Increasing enterprise demand and long sales cycles are blocking revenue. Consistent triage reduces misprovisioning risk and helps standardize downstream engineering work (templates for pool sizing, autoscaling guardrails, and canary rules).
acceptance_criteria: A reusable intake worksheet (Google Sheet or Form) with fields mapping to the scoring rubric is published and linked in the ticket
A triage scoring rubric that yields one of three SLA bands (Gold / Silver / Bronze) based on deterministic answers is documented
GPU fallthrough table (preferred -> acceptable -> fallback) created for common workload archetypes: low-latency chat, high-throughput batch embeddings, and mixed inference
A takeover handoff checklist for engineering with required artifacts (sample load profile, acceptable tail-latency percentile, data residency notes) is produced
Playbook reduces average intake turnaround (time from first customer call to engineering proposal) in simulation from 6 business days to <=3 business days in at least two trial customers
Stakeholders (Sales SE, Solutions Eng, Runtime Eng, Legal) have reviewed and accepted the rubric in an initial review meeting
proposed_flow: 1) Pre-call: SE fills minimal customer intake form; auto-generates a triage score preview
2) Intake call (30-45m): walk through checklist; capture quantitative signals (QPS, avg seq len, 95/99P latency target, burst tolerance, SLA uptime percentage)
3) Triage scoring: apply rubric to classify into SLA band and GPU-family recommendation
4) Draft proposal: PM auto-populates reserved throughput profile + scaling policy draft for engineering review
5) Engineering pre-check: runtime team reviews fallthrough and validates feasibility; revise if needed
6) Delivery: Solutions Eng sends proposal and next steps to customer; update intake dashboard with decision and metrics
tasks: Draft scoring rubric and sample intake form (owner: PM)
Create GPU fallthrough guidance for top 6 workload archetypes (owner: Runtime Eng)
Build a one-page engineering handoff checklist and required artifact template (owner: Solutions Eng)
Run two pilot intake calls with existing enterprise prospects and measure turnaround (owner: PM + SE)
Iterate rubric after pilot feedback and publish canonical playbook in Confluence (owner: PM)
Create dashboard card in Console to track intake->proposal latency per account (owner: Product Analytics)
Follow-up eng spike to validate worst-case tail latency assumptions for recommended GPU families (owner: Runtime Eng, separate ticket if needed)
decisions: Use three SLA bands (Gold: 99.99% uptime SLO + strict p99 latency; Silver: 99.9% + p99.9 guidance; Bronze: best-effort reserved throughput)
Adopt a default burst policy of 20% burst credit for first 90 days unless customer explicitly requests higher tolerance
For low-latency chat with <50ms p95 target recommend H100 family; if quantized model or sequence lengths <512 recommend A100-quantized as acceptable fallback
For high-volume embedding pipelines recommend capacity reserved on A100-class or equivalent with continuous batching enabled; fall back to lower memory GPUs only with explicit model quant profile
If customer can't provide a realistic QPS trace, require a 7-day pilot traffic sample before finalizing GPU family
dependencies: ENG-28921 (runtime: GPU family performance matrix completion)
PM-42000 (pricing: reserved throughput pricing band proposals)
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Customers underreport burstiness causing underprovisioning. Mitigation: require explicit burst tolerance field and default conservative burst credit; schedule 7-day pilot for ambiguous cases
Risk: Runtime team can't validate some fallbacks without perf testing. Mitigation: flag as 'engineering-validate' and run an eng spike before final commitment
Risk: Overly prescriptive playbook slows sales. Mitigation: create two intake modes: 'quick-start' for proof-of-concept and 'enterprise-triage' for contractual SLAs
measurement_plan: Metric A: average days from intake start to engineering proposal (target <= 3 business days)
Metric B: percentage of proposals requiring >1 engineering revision (target <= 15%)
Metric C: pilot-to-production success rate (target >= 85% within 90 days of provisioning)
Metric D: NPS from Solutions Eng after using the playbook (qualitative feedback)
